finding.text: Dark mode is unreadable on the default theme. With `data-theme=auto` on a phone set to dark, `body` text becomes `--fg` (#e8eaed), but `.card`, `.topbar`, buttons and tables keep `background: #fff`: light text on white. Only `data-theme=dark` repaints them (app/web/style.css:1400-1403). Separately, `.topbar a.nav` hard-codes `color: #202124` (style.css:1374), so in dark mode the nav links are dark on #1e1f22.

The Install button disappears after the first navigation. `draw()` empties the top bar and makes a new `InstallButton` on every route change (app/web/app.js:1148-1156). Each one waits for a new `beforeinstallprompt`, but the browser fires that once per page load, and the button from the first draw is already gone. Catch the event once at module level, keep it, and let every `InstallButton` read it. The listener is also attached only after two `/api` awaits (app.js:1125-1127), so it can miss the event entirely.

Leaving a document while editing keeps the lock forever. The `DocStore` socket and its heartbeat `setInterval` are never closed when the page changes. docs.js:1295 clears only the pinger, and `keep_beating` keeps sending `beat` (app/web/DocStore.js:1045). Everyone else sees "X is editing" until that tab closes. Each document you visit also keeps its own reconnecting socket, which breaks "one socket per open document" (requirements 4). Close the store, or at least release the lock, when the doc page is left.

A fresh agent can't continue from the task folder. It holds only requirements.md, past-work.md and a session.jsonl of process samples: no task log, no outcome, no test results. It doesn't record what was actually deployed (staging yes, per the readme's latency numbers; production is unclear), and doesn't name the three commits on `worktree/qf-2` (f0868b4ee, 8effe0b29, 4716e7e03). Close the task with an outcome that links app/readme.md and records the deploy state.

The lock is keyed by user id (app/src/lock.js:848, app/src/doc.js:528). The same person in two tabs can write from both at once, and closing one tab releases nothing while the other is open. That's acceptable for a demo but is not a strict single editor.

Any signed-in user can list, open and edit any document (`GET /api/docs` returns them all, app/src/index.js:751-755; the socket checks only that the doc exists, index.js:823). There is no owner or share check yet.
The session cookie's HMAC is compared with `===` (app/src/session.js:919). A constant-time compare (`crypto.subtle.verify` with an HMAC key) costs one line.

style.css has leftovers: `.row` is defined twice (style.css:1388 and 1394), `textarea.doc` is unused (the textarea is `.doc-text`), and there is a stray minified `.topbar{flex-wrap:wrap}` (style.css:1392).

The header of app/scripts/live.test.mjs:268 says staging works by passing `STAGING_SESSION_SECRET` and `STAGING_COOKIES`, but the script reads neither. Staging is covered by latency.mjs, so the line is stale.

`staging.lew42.com` is a custom domain (app/wrangler.jsonc:1463), so the deploy adds a record to the lew42.com DNS zone. It doesn't touch the "monorepo" Worker, so requirement 6 holds, but the readme could say so in one line.

The new classes (`DocDO`, `UserDO`, `DocStore`, `App`) have no page showing their live instances. The closest thing is the doc page's stats line. `DocStore` is the first `Item.Store` adapter outside the dev server, and public/framework/core/Item/readme.md doesn't link it.
